preferences.summary: Speak directly to Emma and involve Nadine as communication support.
preferences.details: Use a quiet, calm voice, familiar faces, Makaton symbols and communication cards. Avoid lots of people, loud noises and waking her suddenly.

accessibilityNeeds.summary: Uses Makaton symbols and communication cards.
accessibilityNeeds.details: Emma has a mild to moderate learning disability associated with Down syndrome and needs information presented accessibly.

relationships.name: Nadine Barlow
relationships.notes: Emma's sole carer and holder of parental responsibility; her father has not been involved since infancy.

relationships.name: Adam
relationships.notes: Close to Nadine and available as emergency backup.

background.summary: Lives with her mother, who is her sole carer.
Prolonged absence and infection risk have isolated Emma from school friends.
background.details: School sends some work home; there is no return date.

background.summary: Emma is happy and vibrant when well and enjoys music, art, animals, singing and dressing up.
background.details: Taylor Swift, drawing, colouring, Flopsy the soft toy rabbit and favourite films are important sources of comfort. She wants to start dance lessons.

background.summary: Nadine has friends and Emma's uncle for support but is under emotional and financial pressure.
background.details: Maternal grandparents are elderly and in poor health. Nadine is off work and applying for Carer's Allowance.

background.summary: An established paediatric oncology, cardiology, community nursing, Macmillan and primary-care team supports Emma.
background.details: Named contacts are Dr S. Chen (RMCH haematology/oncology), RMCH cardiology, Gemma Walsh (children's community nurse), Blessing Adeyemi (Paediatric Macmillan) and Dr P. Hughes (Withington Medical Practice). School liaison is ongoing.
Decisions are made in Emma's best interests with Nadine's informed consent while Emma's wishes are gathered using communication aids and her evolving capacity is considered.

problems.details: Diagnosed aged five; relapsed after first-line remission and is responding poorly to second-line chemotherapy.
Diagnosed antenatally and associated with a mild to moderate learning disability.
Repaired in infancy; a leak at the repair site is under cardiology review following chemotherapy-related cardiac complications.

entries.summary: Atrioventricular septal defect surgically repaired at four months of age.

procedure.display: Surgical repair of atrioventricular septal defect

entries.outcome: Good initial recovery; the repair-site leak later required renewed cardiology monitoring.

entries.summary: First-line chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukaemia achieved remission.

medication.display: First-line AML chemotherapy regimen (specific agents not recorded)

entries.indication: Acute myeloid leukaemia diagnosed aged five.

entries.summary: Second-line chemotherapy commenced after AML recurrence.

medication.display: Second-line AML chemotherapy regimen (specific agents not recorded)

entries.reasonEnded: Paused pending multidisciplinary review because response was poor and treatment caused cardiac complications.

entries.summary: Admitted to high-dependency care with a PICC line infection.
entries.reason: PICC line infection during second-line chemotherapy.
entries.outcome: Infection treated; the PICC remains in situ and requires checking at every visit.

entries.summary: Staging MRI showed widespread extramedullary AML relapse.

investigation.display: MRI whole body, brain and whole spine with contrast

entries.conclusion: Widespread relapse involving CNS/leptomeninges, left orbit, liver, spleen, kidneys, diffuse marrow and lymph nodes, with no response to second-line chemotherapy and no cord compression or hydrocephalus.

entries.summary: Specialist oncology care established before the current community visit.
entries.reason: Childhood cancer requiring specialist oncology care.
entries.outcome: Under the care of Dr S. Chen and the children's oncology service.

entries.summary: Children and Young People's Advance Care Plan is in progress.
entries.need: Parallel planning for supportive and palliative care needs.
goals: Support care at home for as long as possible
Keep Nadine involved in every decision
Preserve access to familiar people and favourite activities
interventions: Use Emma's communication aids to gather her wishes
Maintain active oncology review alongside supportive and palliative planning
Escalate pain, fever, infection or acute deterioration using the agreed plan
entries.evaluation: Plan remains in progress and unsigned. DNACPR, ceilings of treatment and ReSPECT decisions await MDT and family discussion.

catalogue.synopsis: A child living with cancer whose mother is her sole carer and whose care requires child- and family-centred communication.
